title: AI contracting: Deal velocity can undermine negotiation
desc: Shifts from software or hours toward completed work and bounded prices while warning that speed is not quality-adjusted value.

kps.k: AI-first contracting shifts the proposition from selling software or lawyer time to delivering completed legal work.
kps.d: Crosby’s founders argue that operating a law firm lets them redesign negotiation workflows, employ lawyers and accept responsibility for the result. Their initial focus on high-volume commercial agreements provides repeatable work and client-specific learning opportunities. Covenant offers another transactional-service model, focused on financial institutions. Ironclad represents a distinct route: selling contract lifecycle management software to in-house departments rather than delivering legal services itself. These approaches share a business-speed objective but allocate work and accountability differently.

qs.q: The only way that we could automate this properly was to build our own law firm.
qs.a: Ryan Daniels — Crosby (AI-native law firm) · AI-native providers · 2025

qs.q: They employ lawyers, own liability, and take on the work end to end.
qs.a: Crosby: The Inner Workings of a Neofirm · Market & press · 2026

kps.k: Deal velocity and bounded pricing replace hours worked as the central commercial measures, without eliminating hourly billing everywhere.
kps.d: Crosby seeks faster reviews and fewer negotiation rounds, using cumulative time in Crosby’s hands rather than total elapsed deal time as its principal metric. Daniels describes per-contract pricing as turning fixed staffing costs into flexible expenditure. Berrent reports Covenant’s two-day, $900 LPA review, alongside a small, declining hourly component for additional work such as negotiation. The practical proposition combines predictable purchasing with incentives to reduce effort; it does not establish that traditional firms deliberately prolong work or that all transactional services fit fixed fees.

qs.q: If you add up all the time that Crosby has spent looking at a contract, that’s our north star metric.
qs.a: Deal Velocity, Not Billable Hours: How Crosby Uses AI to Redefine Legal Contracting — publisher's transcript · AI-native providers · 2025

qs.q: You know the core product you send us an at LPA we review it in two days is $900.
qs.a: Jen Berrent — Covenant (founder) on what makes a firm 'AI-first' · AI-native providers · 2025

kps.k: Reported speed gains remain heterogeneous and do not establish comparable, quality-adjusted productivity improvements.
kps.d: Crosby’s founders report reviews returned within one or two hours and, in the publisher’s transcript, median review times just under an hour. Seah observed a four-minute-fifty-three-second NDA review, compared with an approximately 58-minute unaided baseline supplied by a team member; she explicitly limits the example to a known sample and one contract type. Ironclad’s speaker claims 80% faster turnaround but supplies no methods or underlying data. These figures measure different activities and cannot support a performance ranking. Crosby’s financing and client-contract revenue milestones likewise indicate commercial activity, not independently measured productivity or legal quality.

qs.q: And structuring ourselves with lawyers in the loop in a really clever way allows us to have the oversight of lawyers and kind of all the safety and the quality that I mentioned before, but see how much we can really push the limits on right now we do a contract review and median times are at a little under an hour.
qs.a: Deal Velocity, Not Billable Hours: How Crosby Uses AI to Redefine Legal Contracting — publisher's transcript · AI-native providers · 2025

qs.q: He finished the Non Disclosure Agreement in four minutes and fifty-three seconds with the help of an internal AI redlining harness.
qs.a: Crosby: The Inner Workings of a Neofirm · Market & press · 2026

kps.k: Optimising speed creates a recognised risk of sacrificing clients’ negotiating interests.
kps.d: Huang challenges whether Crosby’s turnaround target could encourage excessive concessions. Sarihan responds that quality guardrails must cover substantive legal work, client risk preferences and negotiating interests, with lawyers and engineers dedicated to those measures. The supplied material does not disclose the guardrail formula or demonstrate its effectiveness. Crosby also reports malpractice insurance, liability for its work and escalation to lawyers. Its current proposition therefore involves supervised automation and professional accountability, not autonomous review; speed alone cannot demonstrate successful delivery.

qs.q: So how do you make sure that you’re not giving in on your customers negotiating leverage in order to kind of maximize that north star?
qs.a: Deal Velocity, Not Billable Hours: How Crosby Uses AI to Redefine Legal Contracting — publisher's transcript · AI-native providers · 2025

qs.q: But I think the key here is knowing exactly when to escalate something up to a lawyer and to get their thumbs up and to know that that liability is covered.
qs.a: Ryan Daniels & John Sarihan (Crosby) — Sequoia Training Data Ep.61 · AI-native providers · 2026

kps.k: Business context and human–AI task allocation matter as much as document generation.
kps.d: Daniels argues that effective negotiation requires deal priorities, previous concessions and knowledge of the client’s business, captured through interfaces and integrations and delivered at the relevant workflow stage. Crosby also reports using AI explanations to help counterparties understand edits. Yet Daniels identifies redlining and routing work between models and lawyers as unresolved technical challenges; his benchmark references lack named tests or numerical results. Seah’s account of engineer shadowing and predictive routing supports the organisational mechanism, not a measured causal effect. The practical emphasis falls on context collection, lawyer-labelled evaluation sets and operational design rather than model capability alone.

qs.q: For contract negotiation, it sounds simple,  it's a legal negotiation, but we have to plug into a CRM and know who are the counter parties, what is the priority of this deal, what are the things that we have given on in the past for deals like this.
qs.a: Ryan Daniels — Crosby (legal services in the age of AI) · AI-native providers · 2026

qs.q: They developed an in-house internal routing “brain” that calculates supply and demand based on predictive models of outages and seasonality.
qs.a: Crosby: The Inner Workings of a Neofirm · Market & press · 2026

kps.k: The model seeks to expand expert capacity, but its implications for legal careers remain unsettled.
kps.d: Daniels reports clients retaining headcount while avoiding additional hiring; the example of two lawyers supposedly replacing a need for 20 is a client’s counterfactual estimate, not measured displacement. The Sequoia discussion also raises concerns about junior-associate and paralegal opportunities. Within Crosby, lawyers build taxonomies, label data and shape products as well as negotiate. Seah reports a deliberate preference for lawyers directing automation rather than merely proofreading it, and conditionally argues that removing routine tasks could strengthen client relationships. Explicit explanation and product collaboration emerge as proposed skills, not proof that automation will improve every lawyer’s role.

qs.q: And one of their lawyers said without Crosby, we'd be 20 lawyers today, which like the ratio is um I mean I think sorry, they're like over 80 sales people now.
qs.a: Ryan Daniels — Crosby (AI-native law firm) · AI-native providers · 2025

qs.q: >> You know, I think coming back to the  point on taste, increasing the leverage of these senior partners at law firms, I get a little worried about, you know, the junior associates and the parallegals and the opportunity for them.
qs.a: Ryan Daniels & John Sarihan (Crosby) — Sequoia Training Data Ep.61 · AI-native providers · 2026

kps.k: Expansion beyond routine contracting is a strategic hypothesis, contested by incumbent investment and general-purpose AI.
kps.d: Berrent argues that much transactional work need not pass through large firms. Daniels predicts growth for automation-led providers while reserving high-value M&A and high-stakes litigation for traditional specialists. Crosby’s ambitions include reusable clause models, negotiation simulation and service for neglected agreements; none establishes autonomous capability across those markets. Seah highlights foundation-model competition and major incumbent technology investment, while Daniels acknowledges that ChatGPT may handle some previously unreviewed work. Hopes of wider access and dramatically higher throughput remain aspirations, distinct from demonstrated enterprise savings or a concrete access-to-justice programme.

qs.q: I think a lot of work runs through big law firms that does not need to run through big law firms.
qs.a: Jen Berrent — Covenant (founder) on what makes a firm 'AI-first' · AI-native providers · 2025

qs.q: I think they'll still command the most uh um coveted parts of the market, the most high value M&A, high stakes litigation.
qs.a: Ryan Daniels — Crosby (AI-native law firm) · AI-native providers · 2025

vlens.an: The legal-tech vendor source constructively shifts the proposition away from AI-first providers delivering completed legal work at bounded prices and toward contract-lifecycle-management software used by in-house legal departments. It shares the cluster’s objective of faster contracting and presents an asserted 80% turnaround improvement as an established business benefit, but it does not engage with the principal warning that speed may reduce quality-adjusted value by weakening negotiation outcomes. Instead, its account centres on software-enabled augmentation: reducing document manipulation, relieving overworked in-house teams and freeing lawyers for legal thinking. There is some internal variation in emphasis: the vendor speaker makes a strong, though methodologically unsupported, performance claim, while the interviewer frames automation more cautiously as a desirable intermediate phase in which lawyers remain in the loop. Neither addresses concessions, negotiating leverage, substantive quality guardrails or provider accountability. This assessment concerns this curated vendor source only and should not be generalized to legal-tech vendors as a group.

qs.q: And the benefits that we have proven at this point is, one, speed, those lawyers can turn around contracts 80% faster, which is a tremendous result for the business because one of the things that we talk about at Ironclad a lot, and I think our customers really appreciate, is behind every business process is a contract process.
qs.a: The Rise of the Legal Technologist · Legal-tech vendor · 2026

qs.q: And I kind of just think that we're going to have a different interface over the same type of tooling, which is going to be much more human centric and allow lawyers to spend more time practicing law and doing the legal thinking as opposed to the document manipulation.
qs.a: The Rise of the Legal Technologist · Legal-tech vendor · 2026

vlens.an: The curated AI-native legal-provider sources support the proposition that contracting can shift from selling software or billable time toward delivery of completed work, with speed and bounded pricing as central commercial measures—but not as substitutes for quality-adjusted value. Crosby’s founders ground this support in an integrated law-firm model that accepts responsibility for contract work, uses AI to accelerate reviews and reduce negotiation rounds, and retains lawyers for judgment, escalation and liability. They expressly recognise that speed-focused incentives can produce shortcuts or weaken clients’ negotiating positions, so they add business-context integration, lawyer oversight and quality guardrails. Material internal variation concerns scope rather than overall direction: Covenant chiefly supports the pricing and provider-model shift through a fixed-price LPA review while retaining limited hourly billing for add-ons, but does not substantively address the negotiation-quality risk; Crosby addresses that risk directly and describes a more developed human–AI operating model. Across both, reported performance evidence is largely founder-reported, anecdotal or operational, so it supports the business-model rationale more strongly than independently verified, comparable productivity or legal-quality gains. These sources are a curated selection and should not be treated as representative of all AI-native legal providers.

qs.q: The only way that we could automate this properly was to build our own law firm.
qs.a: Ryan Daniels — Crosby (AI-native law firm) · AI-native providers · 2025

qs.q: And the reason that matters so much is because it’s very easy to get misaligned incentives of, like, taking shortcuts, or doing work that’s, like, halfway there.
qs.a: Deal Velocity, Not Billable Hours: How Crosby Uses AI to Redefine Legal Contracting — publisher's transcript · AI-native providers · 2025

vlens.an: Within this curated professional voice, Nicole Seah’s profile supports the proposition that AI-first contracting can shift value from selling software or lawyer time toward accountable, end-to-end legal delivery, while speed alone does not establish quality-adjusted value. Crosby’s employment of lawyers, assumption of liability and ownership of the work align directly with the delivery-model claim. Seah also treats the observed 10x NDA-review gain cautiously: it was a narrow internal trial involving a known sample and one contract type, not evidence of performance across live negotiations or of preserved client outcomes. Material variation within the account lies between optimism about lawyer-directed automation, stronger relational work and integrated lawyer-engineer operations, and uncertainty about real-world trust, negotiating quality, scalability and longer-term agentic ambitions. Because the evidence comes from one selected profile, it should not be read as representative of market analysts, consultancies and press generally.

qs.q: They employ lawyers, own liability, and take on the work end to end.
qs.a: Crosby: The Inner Workings of a Neofirm · Market & press · 2026

qs.q: That day the productivity lift was 10x, though in a sterile environment: a known sample, one contract type.
qs.a: Crosby: The Inner Workings of a Neofirm · Market & press · 2026

elens.an: The curated 2025 sources collectively support the proposition that AI-first contracting is shifting value from software licences or lawyer hours toward completed legal work, faster deal progression and bounded pricing, while leaving quality dependent on human oversight and safeguards. Daniels and the Crosby publisher transcript support the proposition most fully: Crosby assumes responsibility for contract work through an integrated law-firm model, treats handling time as a principal metric, and recognises that speed incentives can encourage shortcuts or concessions contrary to clients’ negotiating interests. They therefore frame current delivery as lawyer-in-the-loop augmentation rather than autonomous contracting. Berrent supports the commercial-model component through Covenant’s fixed-price, two-day LPA review and its effort to move suitable transactional work away from large firms, but she retains hourly pricing for some negotiation and does not address the proposition’s quality warning. Material variation also concerns the strength of evidence: Crosby reports sub-hour or one-to-two-hour turnaround and describes quality guardrails, but does not provide comparative, quality-adjusted results or disclose guardrail performance; broader productivity, market-expansion and access claims remain predictions or anecdotes rather than demonstrated outcomes.

qs.q: The only way that we could automate this properly was to build our own law firm.
qs.a: Ryan Daniels — Crosby (AI-native law firm) · AI-native providers · 2025

qs.q: And the reason that matters so much is because it’s very easy to get misaligned incentives of, like, taking shortcuts, or doing work that’s, like, halfway there.
qs.a: Deal Velocity, Not Billable Hours: How Crosby Uses AI to Redefine Legal Contracting — publisher's transcript · AI-native providers · 2025

elens.an: The 2026 sources support the proposition that AI contracting is shifting emphasis from selling software or lawyer time toward faster delivery of completed work, while also supporting the warning that velocity alone is not quality-adjusted value. The Crosby accounts commonly justify the model through end-to-end service delivery, workflow automation, business-context integration and provider accountability; lawyer judgment, escalation and liability remain safeguards against sacrificing negotiating interests. Material internal variation concerns both business model and evidentiary confidence. The Ironclad source redirects attention to CLM software used by in-house departments and presents turnaround speed chiefly as an established operational benefit, without examining concessions or negotiation quality. The Crosby sources are more directly aligned but differ in perspective: founder accounts make operational and commercial claims, while Seah’s observational profile expressly limits a reported 10x gain to a known sample and one contract type. Across these curated sources, reported gains are heterogeneous, largely company-reported or narrowly observed, and do not independently establish comparable improvements in legal quality or negotiation outcomes.

qs.q: And it turns out the best way to do this and to automate it is by building an in-house a law firm, understanding how lawyers work and then trying to replace as much of that agentically to get uh contracts closed faster.
